title: Microflicker profiling scratch - short latency flickers during steady QPS
content:
Context:
- Observing very short (5-50ms) sporadic latency spikes during otherwise stable qps runs. Spikes are too small to be classified as microbursts in our usual definition (100ms+), but frequent enough to impact perceived latency jitter for latency-sensitive customers.

Hypothesis (early):
- These 'microflickers' correlate with brief GPU context-switches / driver interrupts during scheduling and with small KV-cache invalidation windows when multiplexing many tenants. Could also be caused by early preemption from background maintenance work (e.g., checkpointing, watcher threads).

Testbed / config:
- Model: llama-13B-quantized-v2 (sequence len 512)
- Hosts: 1x A100-80GB (k8s node) running runtime v0.16.2-rc3
- Containers pinned to GPU using nvidia-container-toolkit, runc shim in use
- Inference runtime config (selected):
  - batch_timeout_ms: 8
  - max_concurrency_per_gpu: 16
  - kv_cache: enabled, prefix caching ON
  - preemption_policy: soft
- Load generator: wrk2 adapted for HTTP streaming (custom client)
- Load profile: steady 250 req/s (each req ~32 tokens generated) for 30 minutes

Commands / snippets used:
- wrk2: ./wrk -t12 -c400 -d1800s -R250 --latency http://gateway.local/v1/gen
- cpu/gpu top sampling: watch -n 0.5 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,compute_mode --format=csv
- kernel messages: sudo journalctl -k -f | grep -i nvidia
- runtime debug: /opt/runtime/bin/telemetry dump --since 2025-07-14T10:00Z --event-sources scheduler,kv,preempt

Representative observations (sampled):
- Overall: mean 22ms p50, p95 43ms, p99 78ms when measured continuous. But there are recurring sub-50ms spikes within the p95->p99 band that look like flickers.

- Extract from latency trace (timestamps are approx):
  2025-07-14T10:12:04.213Z request-id=... latency_ms=21
  2025-07-14T10:12:06.981Z request-id=... latency_ms=37 (flicker)
  2025-07-14T10:12:08.409Z request-id=... latency_ms=19
  2025-07-14T10:12:11.002Z request-id=... latency_ms=46 (flicker)
  2025-07-14T10:12:13.118Z request-id=... latency_ms=18

- GPU telemetry correlates: at the same timestamps we see ~2-4% transient drop in GPU util followed by brief spike in GPU mem usage (+~10MB) and small uptick in PCIe activity. No full GPU reset.

- Kernel / driver messages near flickers:
  Jul 14 10:12:06 host kernel: nvidia: nvidia_drm: waiting for clients to close before reset
  Jul 14 10:12:11 host kernel: nvidia-mig: MIG slice eviction requested (trace id 0x7f)
  (these are noisy but recurring, not full resets)

- Runtime traces: scheduler shows a handful of 'preempt_request' events lasting 3-12ms, and KV cache shows 'prefix-evict' occurring ~every 7-12s (short window). Many of the preempt events align with flicker timestamps.

Micro-investigation experiments run (iterations):
1) Disable KV prefix eviction (force retain)
   - result: microflicker frequency dropped ~45%, p99 moved from 78ms -> 62ms.
2) Increase batch_timeout_ms -> 16ms (slightly larger batching window)
   - result: mean up ~+3ms but flicker incidence reduced ~30% (less scheduler churn).
3) Switch preemption_policy soft -> off (best-effort no preempt)
   - result: flickers nearly disappeared in 10min run; observed occasional background GC-induced spike (120ms) after 12min (tradeoff!).
4) Simulate background maintenance by triggering periodic checkpoint (every 10s)
   - result: introduced 20-150ms spikes large enough to dominate tail; not typical for customers but shows sensitivity to maintenance timing.

Quick charts (described):
- Histogram of latencies: strong mode at 18-24ms, small secondary shoulders at 36-48ms and rare tail >100ms.
- Time series p95/p99 over 30min: p95 stable, p99 shows thin vertical spikes every ~6-12s (matching prefix-evict cadence).

Preliminary conclusions:
- Two independent contributors to microflicker: brief scheduler preemption (3-12ms) and KV-cache micro-evictions that add a small (~10-40ms) penalty when rehydrating prefix context.
- Disabling eviction reduces flickers significantly but risks memory pressure when multi-tenant density grows. Need smarter eviction heuristics (age vs active-window).
- Soft preemption gives us safety but at cost of jitter; disabling preemption reduces jitter but can cause longer single-event GC-like stalls when background work collides.

Actionable next steps / experiments:
- Implement a small experiment on stage: adaptive-evict that favors eviction of prefixes not touched in last N requests (N=300), measure flicker incidence vs memory usage chart (run for 2 hours).
- Add micro-tracing hook on runtime to emit a "flicker-tag" event when a request experiences a latency jump >30% over recent moving median; correlate with GPU driver events.
- Try small pacing layer ahead of scheduler: if incoming stream is highly regular, avoid preemption for running batches unless >Xms pending. Measure throughput/cost.
- File follow-up: ENG-2314 (linked). Draft design for eviction heuristic and gating preemption changes.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Tradeoff surface: jitter vs memory safety vs single-event long stall.
- Customer impact: interactive UIs notice sub-50ms spikes; embedding backfills (throughput jobs) don't care. Consider tiering preemption and eviction per-customer SLA.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Do any GPU driver versions (470.x vs 520.x) show different preemption characteristics? Need matrix test.
- Are these flickers more pronounced for shorter generation lengths (<64 tokens) due to smaller per-request GPU occupancy?
- Is there a relationship with PCIe background transfers (model shard sync) that we haven't captured?

TODO checklist (short):
- [ ] Run 2-hour adaptive-evict job on staging (tag: kiran/adv-evict)
- [ ] Add flicker-tag events to telemetry (small PR) - assign to Noah
- [ ] Run driver-version matrix on A100 nodes (Aisha owns infra tickets)
- [ ] Draft eviction heuristic doc and get 1:1 with runtime PM

Random scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Could we do tiny per-tenant soft-affinity windows to avoid eviction of the last N prefixes for recently active tenants? Low overhead bloom filter to track recency.
- Introduce micro-sleep (200-400us) between scheduler slices to allow GPU driver housekeeping to run asynchronously rather than inline with work. Risk: added mean latency but may flatten flicker amplitude.

Bottom line (current):
- Microflicker exists and is material for interactive SLAs. We have short-term knobs (disable eviction, disable preempt) that reduce flickers but add other risks. Longer-term fix likely requires smarter eviction + scheduler pacing and better coordination with GPU driver housekeeping.
